text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton will be in Greece and Turkey in June to discuss Greco-Turkish disputes and Cyprus.
- Greece's Defence Minister Akis Tsohatzopoulos promises a strong Greece able to provide air cover for Cyprus in the event of a Turkish offensive on the island.
- Turkey adopts a silent wait-and-see attitude to forthcoming initiatives on the Cyprus problem, keeping its position on key issues under wraps.
- A new meeting on whether cost of living allowances should be paid by employers has been set for Thursday.
- Prostitution rackets and drug trafficking is the root of crime in Limassol, police believe.
- Defence ministers of Cyprus and Greece dismiss suggestions of a ban in Greek airforce jets flying over Cyprus.
- Multi-million pound tunnel on Limassol - Paphos highway is ready but it will not be opened because of delays in installing lighting system.
- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash seeks a dialogue through letters with President Clerides.
